analysis.title: Connecting the Dots: Sell-off, US Midterms, Data centers and Conviction List plus key research
key_insights: The initial US sell-off after the Democratic midterm sweep spread beyond data-center-related names to the index level. Owners of existing compute were seen as relative beneficiaries of a data center slowdown because of lower supply.

Aterio expert call revisited: Texas is 26% of 2026-2030 US data center net additions, and most of the announced pipeline is not under construction. Michael Ng frames risks to his US DC forecasts but thinks they are conservative.

Aterio's 'under construction' definition includes site works such as land clearing, which developers usually do before securing an electricity services agreement or air permits. A moratorium can therefore affect projects counted as under construction.

Investors are debating whether a US data center slowdown helps Europe. Alberto Gandolfi argues Europe has a real DC opportunity, judged name by name given execution risk, with Solaria (Buy, Conviction List) a potential beneficiary and a CMD on 19 Nov.

November European Conviction List: Carlsberg and Deutsche Bank added, HSBC, Haleon and CTP removed. Upside to consensus earnings is one screening criterion. US list adds Amphenol. APAC list adds Elite Material, Yokohama Rubber and JSW Steel and removes NYPCB, Shengyi Tech and Hong Kong Exchanges.

Rating changes: BAT upgraded to Buy and Imperial reiterated Buy, both with 22% PT upside on nicotine's defensive qualities and margins. Kuehne & Nagel cut to Neutral on a narrowed gap to consensus. Gecina cut to Neutral with GSe 27/28 EPS 3-4% below Visible Alpha consensus.

Credit and AI: $568 billion of AI-related financing in global IG syndicated credit so far this year, $40bn in recent days. Hyperscaler lease commitments are $1.7tn, 75% for leases not yet begun. Supply has passed GS's full-year 2026 forecast of $250bn and EUR IG AI issuance is accelerating.

US Midterms: utilities and renewables were the key debate. GS sees the outcome as likely positive overall for US renewable activity including Orsted and EDPR. Merlin Properties' European DC positioning looks better post midterms.
Power constraints: US September capacity additions accelerated, led by solar and storage. Labor availability is a key constraint on AI and data center power demand growth.

Europe earnings: GS raises STOXX 600 EPS growth forecasts to 18% for 2026 and 7% for 2027 and adds 5% for 2028, above economic growth because global growth matters more. US earnings growth is strong but no longer accelerating.

Tech earnings: Arista beat on EPS, revenue and margin and guided 2026 revenue +48% YoY at the midpoint. AMD sees strong revenue growth through 2027 versus lowered investor expectations. Apple beat on iPhone and Mac revenue but memory and inference costs pressure gross margins and the outlook.

Transport and industrial results: Maersk fell 6% on a 3Q miss and lowered guidance, and was cut to Sell. IAG's 3Q26 EBIT was 5% below company-compiled consensus. Lufthansa cut the top end of guidance. Heidelberg Materials rose 10% on a 3% EBIT beat. Legrand beat and raised with 9M26 data center growth around 40%.

Rheinmetall cut guidance on delays in Arminius project awards, implying roughly 5% cuts to FY26 consensus sales and 8% to operating earnings. Nordex is seen pointing to further consensus upgrades (GSe 12.3% margin versus 11% consensus).

Commodities: Brent forecasts raised to $105/bbl for Dec 2026 (from $90) and $88 for 2027 (from $80) on supply disruption risk. Gold end-2026 forecast cut to $4,150/toz and end-2027 to $4,800 (from $5,400) on the Fed's hawkish shift and positioning, with a structurally constructive longer-term view on central bank demand. 2027 TTF gas forecast raised. Chile copper labour talks add 2027 supply risk, most relevant to BHP, RIO, LUN and ANTO.

Crypto: Binance disclosed a cybersecurity incident on 29 Oct, the largest to date by affected assets. $19.9bn or 14% of assets have left the platform. GS says this questions cybersecurity across the crypto ecosystem and could affect long-term industry growth.

Macro: the BOE hiked as expected and its communication supports another hike in February, with December possible. German retail sales weakened further. 2027 fiscal impulse is roughly neutral across major economies, with risks to growth skewed down. China CIO tour: persistent fiscal tightening, no leadership appetite for a property rebound, expected growth slowdown.

Events and M&A: Coca-Cola HBC fell 18% on press reports of a Russian petition to place its Russian operations under external administration. BT rose 7% on speculation VMO2 plans to rent BT fibre. Puig reportedly among suitors for Parfums de Marly. Omnicom is the main winner in Lidl's EU media review. Bayer won the Aretino jury trial.

Consumer and healthcare: Next full price sales +8% YoY with international revenue +32%. Essity and Magnum Ice Cream are Sell ideas on cost inflation hitting margins. Novo's FY27 could be another transition year, with the CFO leaving. Sanofi had a strong beat and raise helped by one-offs and phasing.

market_movers.rationale: BAT upgraded to Buy with 22% PT upside. Higher quality growth story with accelerating New Categories and defensive nicotine economics.
Imperial Brands reiterated Buy with 22% PT upside on best-in-class margins amid input cost uncertainty.
Kuehne & Nagel cut to Neutral with an unchanged target. Shares outperformed, the gap to consensus has narrowed, and the 2027 container cooling view is less differentiated.
Gecina cut to Neutral on lower forecasts after an asset tour, with longer letting times and lower rental reversion. GSe 27/28 EPS is 3-4% below consensus.
Carlsberg added to the European Conviction List on solid topline growth, soft drink trends and deleveraging progress.
Deutsche Bank added to the European Conviction List on improving revenue momentum in Corporate and Private bank and German momentum.
Amphenol added to the US Conviction List.
Solaria is a Buy on the Conviction List and a potential European data center beneficiary, with a CMD on 19 Nov.
Drax rose 7% on a strategic partnership for more than 1GW of data centre capacity. CMD on 23 Nov is the next catalyst.
Merlin Properties focused on its data center programme, especially Lisbon. Spanish regulatory risk has reduced.
Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are Buys after Kioxia's CY3Q read-across, with the medium- to long-term NAND outlook intact.
Maersk fell 6% on a 3Q miss and revised guidance, with lower container volumes and higher bunker and network costs. GS says it is as good as it gets for the container market.
In-line 3Q with faster organic growth but lower margins. Focus is on the CMD and new mid-term targets.
Heidelberg Materials rose 10% on 9% EBIT growth, a 3% beat, with resilient volumes and solid pricing power.
IAG 3Q26 EBIT of 1.73bn euros was 5% below company-compiled consensus, partly on disruption costs.
Ryanair rose 5% on results. GSe FY27 net income edges up on better near-term fares, 1% ahead of VA consensus, while FY28E is 25% below on fuel prices.
Lufthansa rose 4% on a solid 3Q but the top end of guidance was reduced. Consensus is likely to stay in the lower half of the range.
IMCD organic gross profit growth improved to 9.6% in 3Q26 from 7.3%, helped by APAC. On the Conviction List.
Strong revenue growth outlook through 2027 versus investor expectations lowered after Intel's report. Data center underpins growth despite PC headwinds.
3Q EPS, revenue and margin beat, 2026 revenue guided +48% YoY at the midpoint, and a strong initial 2027 outlook.
iPhone and Mac revenue beat showed pricing power, but memory and inference costs weigh on the outlook and gross margins.
Scout24 rose 7% post results, with limited consensus changes and a PEG below 1x. On the Conviction List.
BT Group beat on Openreach growth. GS expects rising free cash flow and consensus beats to drive a re-rating and higher shareholder returns. On the Conviction List.
Deutsche Telekom had a modest beat and a small buyback disappointment, with investor focus on US satellite risk.
Auto1 broadly in line, with growing evidence of a growth re-acceleration at higher gross profit per unit.
Rightmove guides FY27 revenue growth similar to FY26 in a challenging market, so GS lowers operating profit estimates.
Auto Trader's Retailer Revenue fell 1% against an expected flat 1H27, so GS trims FY28E Retailer Revenue by 1-2%.
JCDecaux had a slight 3Q organic growth beat and slightly ahead 4Q guidance.
Rheinmetall cut guidance on Arminius award delays, implying about 5% cuts to FY26 consensus sales and 8% to operating earnings. 3Q profit beat. On the Conviction List.
Legrand beat and raised with 9M26 data center growth around 40% versus over 30% in 1H26. Shares were flat.
Wartsila CMD focus is capital allocation after higher long-term targets. Recently upgraded to Buy.
Nordex had strong results with excellent execution. GSe 12.3% margin versus 11% consensus points to further upgrades.
Saudi Aramco beat on net income with strong cash flow generation.
Viridien rose 3% on results with early signs of a seismic recovery. Read-across positive for TGS.
Tenaris had a strong 3Q on Middle East recovery and US pricing, but GS stays Neutral on valuation.
Weir fell 10% on soft organic order intake growth versus peers and the acceleration needed to meet FY26 consensus.
Lanxess rose 6% on in-line EBITDA including tariff one-offs, but the implied 4Q looks demanding.
Vonovia's revised guidance brings capital allocation into focus, with socialization risk still present.
IWG results show capital light execution. GS raises FY26-30 EPS 2-7% on upgraded guidance.
Unilever CMD: focus on being a pure play HPC company, US growth driver, India penetration headroom, margin upside versus peers.
Zalando fell 6% on in-line results after outperforming into them. GMV growth improved sequentially.
Marks & Spencer Food momentum is impressive and availability issues are resolved. CMD next week.
Next: full price sales +8% YoY and international revenue +32% as marketing spend rose 67%.
Barry Callebaut rose 9% post results with minimal consensus changes expected.
FY27 could be another transition year, with upside if the Wegovy pill ex-US drives growth. CFO leaving after 27 years.
Bayer rose 4% on results. Pharma is entering a new growth phase (Kerendia, Nubeqa) while Crop stays volatile.
3Q strong beat and raise, but underlying strength was supported by one-offs, phasing and cost control.
Smith & Nephew had mixed 3Q results with unexpected softness in Wound. Strategic options in focus.
Philips rose 5% on strong orders and resilient margins. D&T growth is the next unlock.
LVMH: GS is optimistic on Fashion & Leather as the LV brand transition weighs less, Dior improves and the rest of the division grows strongly.
Current valuation fails to reflect the growth opportunity and multiple high-potential 2027 catalysts.
Halma's Photonics weakness: applying a 10-year median P/E of about 30x to ex-Photonics EPS implies Photonics is valued below 8x. FY results 19 Nov. On the Conviction List.
Essity's constrained pricing power leaves margins vulnerable to cost inflation.
Magnum Ice Cream: cost inflation weighs on 2027 margin expansion and volume growth.
Alstom: numbers cut materially after a profit warning and still below medium-term guidance. EV/Sales of 0.36x is not at trough of 0.17x.
RWE won 2GW across three CCGTs, with another auction in December and potential DC deals. On the Conviction List.
British Land's cost restructuring and management business spin-off could have a positive EPS impact.
Puig is reportedly among suitors for Parfums de Marly. GS takes no view on probability but sees it as strategically consistent. On the Conviction List.
Volvo Group roadshow: North American underlying fleet demand is solid despite EPA17 uncertainty.
EDP has a new CEO ahead, with strategic questions on capital raising, Brazil, data centers and consolidation. EDPR is Buy.
Flatex app downloads up 46% MoM in October. On the Conviction List.

sector_views.rationale: Pipeline is concentrated in Texas and mostly announced rather than under construction. Credit supply for AI is rising fast, so GS frames risks to the buildout while staying constructive on named beneficiaries.
GS raises STOXX 600 EPS growth forecasts to 18% for 2026 and 7% for 2027 because global growth matters more than the local economy.
Maersk cut to Sell. GS sees a cooling container market in 2027 and notes higher costs.
Mixed 3Q: IAG missed consensus, Lufthansa trimmed guidance, Ryanair had better near-term fares but FY28 fuel risk.
Midterm outcome seen as likely positive overall for US renewable activity, with RWE and EDPR catalysts ahead.
Essity and Magnum are Sells on cost inflation and constrained pricing power, while BAT and Imperial are favored for defensiveness.
Binance security incident with 14% of assets leaving the platform calls ecosystem cybersecurity into question.
German defence spending is lifting equipment investment, but Rheinmetall cut guidance on award delays.

earnings_insights: Arista 3Q: EPS, revenue and margin beat (reported), 2026 revenue guided +48% YoY at the midpoint, strong initial 2027 outlook.
Apple fiscal quarter: iPhone and Mac revenue beat (reported). Gross margins pressured by memory cost inflation, partly offset by higher ASPs and inventory management.
AMD: GS sees strong revenue growth through 2027 versus investor expectations that were lowered after Intel reported last week.
IAG 3Q26 EBIT 1.73bn euros (reported) versus company-compiled consensus 1.81bn euros, a 5% miss, partly on disruption costs.
Heidelberg Materials: 9% EBIT growth (reported), a 3% beat versus consensus, shares +10%.
Legrand: beat and raise, 9M26 data center growth c.40% versus over 30% at 1H26, implying FY26 consensus rises by a low-single-digit percent.
Rheinmetall pre-release: guidance cut implies about 5% cuts to FY26 consensus sales and 8% to operating earnings, while 3Q profit beat.
Nordex: GSe 12.3% margin versus consensus 11% for FY27, pointing to further upgrades.
Ryanair: GSe FY27 net income raised slightly, 1% ahead of Visible Alpha consensus, while FY28E is 25% below consensus because fuel prices are not fully in models.
Maersk 3Q: miss versus expectations with revised guidance, shares down 6%.
Lufthansa 3Q: solid results but the top end of guidance was reduced, shares +4%.
IMCD: 3Q26 organic gross profit growth 9.6% (reported) versus 7.3% in 2Q26, APAC 20.1% versus 7%.
Sanofi 3Q: strong beat and raise, with underlying strength helped by one-offs, phasing and cost control.
Lanxess: EBITDA in line (reported) including one-offs from US tariffs, FY guidance narrowed to the upper end of the range.
Weir: shares -10% on soft organic order intake growth versus peers.
Next: full price sales +8% YoY and international revenue +32% (reported), marketing spend +67% YoY.
Auto Trader: Retailer Revenue fell 1% in 1H27 versus GS's flat expectation (reported). GS trims FY28E Retailer Revenue by 1-2%.
US earnings season: growth is strong but no longer accelerating, per Ben Snider.
Upcoming: Halma FY results 19 Nov, Solaria CMD 19 Nov, Drax CMD 23 Nov, Marks & Spencer CMD next week, Alstom CMD in 2Q27.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS expects another hike in February, December possible. Risks to its two-hike baseline, which is below market pricing, lean toward more tightening.
Forecast raised on high supply disruption risks.
Higher oil price path on supply risks.
Lowered because the Fed's recent hawkish shift affects positioning.
Still constructive longer term on structurally strong central bank demand.
Earnings growth above economic growth because global growth matters more.
Expansion in Germany and Japan offsets consolidation in the UK, with the US flat. Growth risks skew to the downside.
Issuance has run above GS's full-year forecast of $250bn for hyperscaler debt supply.
Confirms softening consumption momentum into winter.

crypto_views: Binance disclosed a cybersecurity incident on 29 Oct, the largest to date by affected assets.
$19.9bn or 14% of Binance's assets have left the platform.
GS says the incident calls into question cybersecurity across the crypto ecosystem and could affect long-term industry growth (James Yaro).

trade_ideas.rationale: Constrained pricing power leaves margins vulnerable to cost inflation.
Cost inflation weighs on 2027 margin expansion and volume growth.
3Q miss and revised guidance, and the container market is seen at peak.

trade_ideas.description: Buy Solaria as a European data center beneficiary ahead of the 19 Nov CMD
trade_ideas.rationale: Europe has a significant DC opportunity and Solaria is on the Conviction List.
22% PT upside on defensive nicotine economics and best-in-class margins.

risk_factors: A US data center slowdown, with most of the announced pipeline not under construction and a moratorium able to affect projects counted as under construction.
Concentration of the data center pipeline in Texas.
Labor availability constraining AI and data center power demand growth.
Rising AI-related debt supply and off balance sheet hyperscaler lease commitments of $1.7tn.
Memory cost inflation pressuring Apple's gross margins.
Hawkish Fed shift weighing on gold positioning.
Fiscal deficits skewing growth risks to the downside.
Crypto exchange cybersecurity risk after the Binance incident.
Supply disruption risk for oil and gas, and Chile copper labour negotiations.
Input and cost inflation hitting consumer staples margins.
Execution risk on European data center projects.
US earnings growth is no longer accelerating.
vol_and_positioning: The post-midterm sell-off spread from data center-related names to the index level.
Owners of current compute were seen as relative beneficiaries of a data center slowdown.
Gold forecast cut on the implications of the Fed's hawkish shift for positioning.
Luxury: investors are cautious and many do not expect US demand to accelerate sequentially this quarter.
geopolitical: US midterm elections produced a Democratic sweep that the report calls a blue tsunami, with implications for utilities, renewables and data center policy.
Reports that a local beverage producer petitioned Russian authorities to place Coca-Cola HBC's Russian operations under external administration.
High supply disruption risks cited as the reason for raising Brent forecasts.
Chile labour negotiations add a copper supply risk into 2027.
Germany defence spending is driving a pick-up in equipment investment.
China CIO Macro Tour: leadership has no desire to see a property rebound and will need to manage a large and rising trade surplus.
US tariffs produced one-offs in Lanxess's results.

tension_points.bear_case: Texas is 26% of the 2026-2030 US pipeline and most of it is announced rather than under construction. Site works counted as construction mean a moratorium can hit under-construction projects too.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Catalysts named are Solaria's CMD on 19 Nov and Drax's CMD on 23 Nov, which test the European DC opportunity.

tension_points.bull_case: GS raises STOXX 600 EPS growth to 18% for 2026 and 7% for 2027 because global growth matters more than the local economy.
tension_points.bear_case: Fiscal impulse is roughly neutral in 2027 and risks to growth are skewed to the downside. German retail sales weakened further.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings growth is strong and market breadth has partly improved through catch up and catch down.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth is no longer accelerating, which is the fundamental challenge for equity investors.
